trigger: argv construction for an external `codex exec` subprocess + config-file parsing that feeds it (security-sensitive surface; prior round had HIGH/MEDIUM argv-injection + Windows .cmd-shim findings)

doubts.claim_under_doubt: a malicious or malformed shipwright_model_config.json can't do anything worse than get its bad value rejected
doubts.disproof_attempt: The value IS rejected -- and then re-emitted verbatim, unescaped and uncapped, into a string the dispatch doc instructs the driving LLM to paste into a shell command line via --transport-note/--disposition double-quoted arguments.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Stop echoing the raw value in the error message, and/or route it through the syntactic allowlist earlier.
doubts.disposition: fixed: CodexReviewTransportError no longer echoes the raw value at all -- reports the pattern and value length only. New test_hostile_config_value_hard_errors_and_does_not_echo_it asserts the hostile string and any '"' are absent from result["reason"].

doubts.disproof_attempt: Safety depends on every caller using .fullmatch(), not on the pattern itself (^...$ lets a trailing newline through under .match()). The test characterising the pattern itself used the unsafe .match() form.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Change the pattern to \A...\Z so .match() and .fullmatch() are equivalent.
doubts.disposition: fixed: pattern changed to \A[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}\Z. test_real_codex_model_slugs_pass_the_allowlist switched to .fullmatch().

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the precedence chain can't be confused or bypassed -- every layer's bad value is rejected
doubts.disproof_attempt: The config layer (attacker-reachable via a PR, not just an operator's own flag) had no test proving a hostile value there hard-errors without launching codex exec.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: One test mirroring test_hostile_codex_model_flag_hard_errors but via shipwright_model_config.json.
doubts.disposition: fixed: added test_hostile_config_value_hard_errors_and_does_not_echo_it, asserting exit 1, status error, argv[0] != 'codex', and the hostile value absent from the reason.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the hardcoded default is trusted, so it needs no check
doubts.disproof_attempt: CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL is validated unconditionally now, but no test asserts the constant itself satisfies its own allowlist -- editing the constant could silently produce an invalid default.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Add transport.CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL to the allowlist-pass parametrize list.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the drift test makes a forgotten tier-enumeration site fail loudly
doubts.disproof_attempt: Substring containment catches a MISSING new literal but not a SURVIVING stale one at a multi-occurrence site. Confirmed no such site exists today outside docs/guide.md, which already has its own == 6 count check.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Assert absence of the previous-generation literal, or apply the count check uniformly.
doubts.disposition: disclosed, no code change: documented as a known residual gap in the test module's own docstring -- latent-only risk, disproportionate to close given no live instance.

doubts.disproof_attempt: The code is revertible; a project's shipwright_model_config.json that adopted codex_review/codex_plan_review is not -- reverting produces spurious 'unrecognized key' warnings on every subsequent config read until the key is removed by hand.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Acknowledge in the ADR's Consequences section.
doubts.disposition: disclosed, no code change: added a 'Revert is noisy, not silent' paragraph to the ADR's Consequences section.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: review_via_codex.py prints a structured error for every failure mode, never a traceback
doubts.disproof_attempt: (1) The role-map drift guard was a module-level assert, stripped under python -O, letting a missing role reach a KeyError instead of the promised structured error. (2) review_via_codex.py's local effective_model (pre-fallback, may be None) collided in name with codex_review_transport.py's effective_model (post-fallback, the AC35-required value) -- a trap for the next editor.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Replace the assert with an explicit raise; rename the pre-fallback local.
doubts.disposition: fixed: assert replaced with `if ...: raise RuntimeError(...)`; local renamed to requested_model.

summary: 7 doubts (1 high, 2 medium, 4 low) across all four lenses. All 7 answered in writing before commit: 5 fixed in code, 2 acknowledged and documented (both confirmed latent-only, no live instance). Verified: ruff clean, 110 affected tests pass, all touched files at or under the 300-line cap.
empty_lenses: RANK/RANKED_TIERS floor interaction with the new fable tier -- no KeyError path exists
argv-injection/BatBadBut class for the model value itself -- allowlist forbids shell metacharacters and a leading '-'; fullmatch closes the trailing-newline gap
the precedence chain (--codex-model uses `is not None`, not `or`; plan_review reads its own key) -- no path lets a config value skip validation
the untouched security posture (scrubbed_env, _resolve_codex_binary, symlink write guard, fresh TemporaryDirectory-per-attempt) -- byte-unchanged by this diff
tier-enumeration drift -- grepped the whole tree, no surviving stale enumeration outside intentional prose
